jess_customer: Hey team — after we flipped on the interface endpoint for redwood-api in account-prod we see intermittent 502/504s from our app. Only affects requests from subnet-private-3 (us-east-1c). Started ~6h ago. No changes to app.

maria_support: Sorry to hear that. Can you share a minimal repro (curl) and DNS resolution from one of the failing hosts? Also which endpoint type (Interface) and whether Private DNS was enabled?

jess_customer: repro: 
```
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/health || true
```
From the failing host: `curl` sometimes returns 200, often TLS handshake error: "SSL: certificate subject name '*.redwood.com' does not match 'api.redwood.example.com'" and sometimes 502.

maria_support: hmm cert mismatch intermittently suggests some requests are hitting a public gateway / CDN while others hit the private endpoint. Can you run `dig +short api.redwood.example.com @169.254.169.253` (instance resolver) and `dig +short api.redwood.example.com` from a different subnet for comparison?

jess_customer: outputs: 
- from us-east-1c-host: `54.240.12.32`
- from us-east-1a-host: `10.10.45.98`
So one resolves to a public IP, the other to a private ENI IP.

devon_net: That nails it — split-horizon resolution mismatch. Did you enable "Private DNS" when creating the Interface VPC Endpoint? If not, the host resolver may fall back to public route for some requests. Also check any custom resolver rules forwarding to on-prem.

jess_customer: I thought we enabled it, but let me verify CLI: `aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --vpc-endpoint-ids vpce-0abcd1234 --query 'VpcEndpoints[0].PrivateDnsEnabled'` returned `false`. Oops.

maria_support: ok that explains partial reachability. Two follow-ups: 1) enabling Private DNS will let the normal service hostname resolve to the ENI private IP(s). 2) If you have Route53 resolver rules or an on-prem conditional forwarder, those can still return the public IP — check resolver rules for higher priority.

jess_customer: we do have a conditional forwarder to on-prem for the zone. How do I avoid that taking precedence?

devon_net: resolver rules are matched by rule priority and VPC association order. If your VPC is still using the outbound resolver to on-prem, the query might go there and get the public answer. Two options: associate the private hosted zone for api.redwood.example.com to the VPC and remove the forwarder for that subdomain, or update the resolver rule priority so VPC local resolution wins.

shawn_oncall: also double-check subnet route tables: if some AZs have custom TGW/NAT routing that rewrites DNS or sends traffic out to internet before hitting the ENI, you'll see asymmetric hits. Run `aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=association.subnet-id,Values=subnet-xxxxx` and look for routes pointing at a TGW or IGW covering the service prefix.

jess_customer: checked the RTs — us-east-1c subnets are propagated to TGW and there's a specific route 0.0.0.0/0 -> tgw-123 which sends through central NAT. But the ENI IP (10.10.45.98) is in the same subnet, so host should reach ENI directly.

maria_support: two more quick checks: 1) security group on the VPCE ENI allows your source CIDR; 2) endpoint policy doesn't restrict calls from your account/account-id. `aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters Name=description,Values="AWS PrivateLink: amazonaws.com/*"` and find the ENI -> check SGs.

jess_customer: SG had a rule limiting to the account's prod-range, which is fine. Endpoint policy blank (full). I think the core issue is DNS split-horizon combined with resolver forwarding to on-prem causing flaky public resolution.

maria_support: sounds right. Steps to fix (recommended):
1) Enable Private DNS on the VPCE: `aws ec2 modify-vpc-endpoint --vpc-endpoint-id vpce-0abcd1234 --private-dns-enabled`
2) Create/associate a Route53 private hosted zone for `redwood.example.com` and add A records pointing to the endpoint ENI IPs (or use Alias to the interface endpoint).
3) Update Route53 resolver rules: ensure no conditional forwarder for `redwood.example.com` remains, or set its priority lower than VPC-local.

jess_customer: I enabled Private DNS and associated the PHZ. Also removed the conditional forwarder for that zone on the resolver. Testing now...

deploy-bot: deploy complete: api-mesh routing update v2026.03.17-2

jess_customer: after changes curl from both AZs now returns 200 consistently, no cert errors. No 502s in the last 30 min. Looks fixed. :thumbsup:

maria_support: awesome — thanks for confirming. For completeness: if you ever need a staged rollout, you can add the PHZ association in a canary VPC first and then flip over. Also file a note in your infra runbook about resolver rule precedence — this bit catches folks.

jess_customer: will do. Thanks for the guidance and quick turnaround!

shawn_oncall: marking as resolved. Closing thread in 24h if no regressions.
